text:
Auston Matthews is the captain of a team that has lost four straight, and the week's headlines are about him calling out his teammates after the shutout loss to New Jersey and about what the Leafs would do if he ever left. Meanwhile he has 28 points in 20 games, and his former assistant coach Dave Hakstol called his form "Absolutely dominant."

Both things are true. Toronto takes 57% of the expected goals at five on five with Matthews on, 16 points better than without him: he's the reason the Leafs aren't worse. By our win probability his goals have added more wins than all but seven skaters in the league. But Toronto has also scored 8.4 more goals than expected with him on the ice, which is padding his points, and his ice time has dropped over two minutes a night lately.

Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he played with weak teammates. That hasn't changed. Our range: 31 to 47 goals.
